- If sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.15) over recent days, reduce forecasted price by 2–5% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If model shows a sharp upward spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) followed by a drop, cap the peak at 1.5x the 14-day moving average to prevent overshoot.  
- When sentiment is neutral or slightly positive (avg 0.0–0.15), model tends to overestimate; apply a 1–3% downward bias for 30-day horizon.  
- If recent history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of price decline), model often undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to forecast.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days of sentiment are positive, model tends to lag; adjust forecast to be 1–2% higher than the 14-day moving average.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple negative spikes (e.g., -0.22 or lower), reduce forecast by 3–6% to account for volatility suppression.  
- Avoid forecasting above 85% of the 30-day high unless sentiment is strongly bullish (avg > 0.20) and recent price is trending upward.
